This disruption leads to a spectrum of skeletal dysplasias, including thoracic dysplasia and short ribs, and can be associated with polydactyly.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in DYNC2I2 or DYNC2I1 in individuals with neither disease, or identification of a distinct molecular pathway critical for one disease but not the other. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a high-frequency (AF > 0.01) loss-of-function variant in DYNC2I2 or DYNC2I1 in the general population would challenge the pathogenicity of these genes for rare diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of DYNC2I2 and DYNC2I1 in intraflagellar transport may reveal therapeutic targets for skeletal ciliopathies, potentially involving modulation of cilia function or downstream signaling pathways affected by IFT defects.
